chapter_title: Day 8: Rhodes, From the Colossus to the Knights
learning_objective: The learner will interpret a timeline of the powers that governed Rhodes from 1912 to 1948 to answer which power governed the island at a given date and what followed from it, answering at least 4 of 5 questions correctly on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: timeline **sim-id:** rhodes-changes-hands-1912-1948
**Library:** vis-timeline
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** interpret
**Learning Objective:** The learner will interpret a timeline of the powers that governed Rhodes from 1912 to 1948 to answer which power governed the island at a given date and what followed from it, answering at least 4 of 5 questions correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Ottoman Rhodes, Italian rule of Rhodes, World War II, the Rhodes deportation of 1944, Dodecanese union with Greece (all defined in Part Four above), and the 1923 population exchange (Chapter 7). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers five questions, each locked in before the answer is shown. An answer is correct when it matches the Correct answer column in Content. Mastery is 4 of 5 correct on the first attempt. Scrolling, zooming with buttons, and opening event descriptions are exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Rhodes became Greek when Greece became independent, or after World War I (question 1). (2) Rhodes was occupied by the Axis like Athens, rather than being Axis territory itself (question 2). (3) The deportation happened under Italian rule (question 3). (4) Rhodes passed straight from Germany to Greece (question 4). (5) Rhodes was Greek long before World War II (question 5). **Instructional Rationale:** Interpreting a timeline means reading two kinds of information at once, spans of rule and single events, and relating them. Committing an answer before the reveal makes the learner read the timeline rather than guess from what "feels Greek." **Content:** Rule spans, shown as bands on a single "Who governed Rhodes" row: | Span | Power | |---|---| | 1522 to May 1912 (the band starts off-screen at the left) | Ottoman Empire | | May 1912 to September 1943 | Italy | | September 1943 to May 8, 1945 | Germany (military occupation) | | May 8, 1945 to March 31, 1947 | Britain (military administration) | | March 31, 1947 onward | Greece (Greek administration; formal union March 7, 1948) | Events, shown as points on a second row, each with the one-sentence description shown when opened: | # | Date | Event | Description | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | May 1912 | Italy seizes Rhodes | During the Italo-Turkish War, Italy takes Rhodes and the Dodecanese from the Ottoman Empire, calling it temporary. | | 2 | January 30, 1923 | Greek-Turkish population exchange agreed | Orthodox Christians of Turkey and Muslims of Greece are to be exchanged; Rhodes, Italian, is not included. | | 3 | July 24, 1923 | Treaty of Lausanne | Turkey gives up its claim to the Dodecanese in favor of Italy. | | 4 | 1936 | De Vecchi becomes governor | Italianization of schools and public life intensifies. | | 5 | September 5, 1938 | First anti-Jewish decree on Rhodes | Italy's racial laws reach the island. | | 6 | October 28, 1940 | Greece says "óchi" | Italy invades Greece; Rhodes is an Italian base. | | 7 | April 27, 1941 | German troops enter Athens | The occupation of mainland Greece begins. | | 8 | September 1943 | Italy surrenders; Germans take Rhodes | The German garrison seizes the island from Italian troops. | | 9 | July 23, 1944 | Deportation of the Jews of Rhodes | More than 1,700 people are shipped from the harbor; they reach Auschwitz on August 16, 1944. | | 10 | October 12, 1944 | Athens liberated | German troops leave Athens; Rhodes remains German. | | 11 | May 8, 1945 | Germans surrender the Dodecanese | British military administration begins. | | 12 | February 10, 1947 | Paris peace treaty | Italy cedes the Dodecanese to Greece. | | 13 | March 7, 1948 | Formal union with Greece | Rhodes becomes fully part of the Greek state. | Questions, in this fixed order: | # | Question | Choices | Correct answer | Reason shown after answering | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Which power governed Rhodes when the Greek-Turkish population exchange was agreed in January 1923? | Ottoman Empire; Greece; Italy; Britain | Italy | Italy had held Rhodes since May 1912, so the exchange between Greece and Turkey did not apply there. | | 2 | On October 28, 1940, when Greece said "óchi," which side was Rhodes on? | It was occupied Greek territory; It was Italian territory, an Axis base; It was neutral; It was British | It was Italian territory, an Axis base | Rhodes was part of Italy's empire, so it was on the side attacking Greece. | | 3 | Which power controlled Rhodes when its Jews were deported in July 1944? | Italy; Germany; Britain; Greece | Germany | German forces had held Rhodes since September 1943; the deportation was a German operation, helped by records from the Italian civil administration. | | 4 | Who governed Rhodes between the German surrender and Greek administration? | Italy again; Britain; Turkey; the United Nations | Britain | A British military administration ran the islands from May 1945 until March 1947. | | 5 | In the 100 years before the Paris peace treaty (February 1847 to February 1947), how many years did Rhodes spend under Greek rule? | None; About 10; About 50; About 100 | None | Greek administration began only on March 31, 1947; before that the island was Ottoman, Italian, German, and British. | **Provenance:** Dates from the chapter sections "Italian Rule of Rhodes," "World War II," "The Rhodes Deportation of 1944," and "Dodecanese Union With Greece," and from Chapter 7 (exchange convention, January 30, 1923; Treaty of Lausanne, July 24, 1923). The anti-Jewish decree date (September 5, 1938) and the start of German control (September 1943) are from the timeline of the Fondazione CDEC exhibition "Jews of Rhodes: Eclipse of a Community" (https://ebreidirodi1944.cdec.it/en/timeline-the-historical-context/). The generator must check the date of Greek administration (March 31, 1947) and the German surrender of the Dodecanese (May 8, 1945) against the Wikipedia article "Dodecanese" and flag any difference to the author rather than change the chapter. **Rules:** The timeline runs from January 1910 to December 1949. Rule spans do not overlap; each event falls inside exactly one span, and opening an event names the span it falls in. Question 5: the period ends before Greek administration began on March 31, 1947, so the answer is None. Zoom and pan use buttons, not the mouse wheel. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the two rows, rule spans and events, with all events visible. 2. The learner opens any events to read their descriptions (exploration). 3. The learner answers question 1 by choosing one option; the answer is locked in, the correct answer is shown with its reason, and the relevant event or span is highlighted on the timeline. 4. The learner repeats for questions 2 to 5. 5. The learner should notice that Athens and Rhodes were on opposite sides of the war until 1945, and that Rhodes became Greek only after the war ended. **Feedback:** Five questions, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: ." Incorrect: "Not quite. The answer is : ." A running score "Correct: n of 5" is shown. At the end: if score >= 4, "You can read who governed Rhodes in any year, and why it mattered."; otherwise, "Look again at where 1923, 1940, and 1944 fall among the colored spans." A Try Again option resets the five questions. **Starting State:** Both rows visible from 1910 to 1949, no question answered, and the prompt "Rhodes changed rulers four times in 35 years. Who was in charge when it mattered?" **Chapter Anchors:** Italy seized Rhodes in May 1912; Treaty of Lausanne 1923; De Vecchi from 1936; racial laws 1938; Ochi Day October 28, 1940; Athens fell April 27, 1941; Germans took Rhodes September 1943; deportation July 23, 1944, more than 1,700 people, arrival at Auschwitz August 16, 1944; Athens liberated October 12, 1944; German surrender May 8, 1945; Paris treaty February 10, 1947; formal union March 7, 1948; thirteen events; five questions; mastery 4 of 5.
